output.subject: A newsletter tool built for people who write about code (1,100 beta writers, code blocks that actually render)
output.pitch:
Hey — if your audience includes developers or technical writers running programming newsletters, lettercraft might be worth a mention.

The one-liner: write in Markdown, publish with git push, own every subscriber.

Most technical newsletter writers are fighting Substack or beehiiv every issue — code blocks come out mangled, content is locked in a proprietary editor, and leaving means losing your archive. lettercraft stores posts as Markdown files in a Git repo the writer owns, renders syntax-highlighted and copyable code blocks across 14 email clients (test matrix is public), and exports the full list in one click.

1,100 writers are publishing during beta. Median send-to-inbox time is under 60 seconds for lists under 10k. Free up to 1,000 subscribers.

If that fits your readers, happy to share more or set up a demo: {APP_URL}
warnings: Proof points are beta-stage figures — flag that context if the newsletter author asks for case studies or long-term retention data.
No deliverability stats (open rates, bounce rates) are published yet; avoid implying deliverability superiority beyond the send-time proof point.
No paid-subscription monetization feature exists yet — do not pitch to newsletters focused on paid tiers.
